newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - March 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - March 25.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Tuesday

* During his visit to China, Vice President Al Gore will appear at the signings of two business deals worth nearly $2 billion, including China's purchase of five Boeing 777 jetliners for $685 million.
* Lehman Brothers first quarter net income rose sharply, beating many analysts' estimates.
* Reed-Elsevier said it would acquire MDL Information Systems for $320 million, in order to grow its profitable scientific publishing business.
* Lam Research agreed to buy OnTrack Systems for about $225 million in stock.
* The Dow industrials rallied but technology stocks extended their decline.
* Krupp backed away from an $8 billion hostile takeover bid for German steelmaker Thyssen AG.
* Comsat has hired Morgan Stanley to find a buyer for its satellite dish-making business called RSI.
* Netcom On-Line Communications is adding new more costly services for its business customers.
* Auction house Christie's signed a 30-year lease for space in the Rockerfeller Center for undisclosed terms.

* Nike, to fend off claims its goods are made in Asian sweatshops, is looking to Andrew Young, former mayor of Atlanta and United Nations representative, and his Goodworks International consulting firm to review the company's international labor code.
* Market place: Variable annuities, a new investment vehicle, also have their risks.
* Treasury prices finished higher ahead of a Federal Reserve meeting.
* A lack of advertising revenue is starting to hurt publishers on the World Wide Web.
* Advertising agency Leo Burnett now faces key rebuilding decisions after its recent management shake-up.
